body: OWNER SCOPE CORRECTION — Sherlock is for local scientific secondary analysis, not redistribution. The owner states that no new consent or provenance gate is wanted: Chen already used these data in published work, and this repository will not redistribute the video, annotations, or recall transcripts. Primary records independently confirm Chen et al. 2017 as the 17-person Sherlock viewing/unguided-recall experiment with 1,000 independently coded semantic segments (DOI 10.1038/nn.4450); the public ContextLab repository states it contains all data analyzed in the later Heusser et al. paper, including raw annotations and recall transcripts; and Zenodo v1.3 publicly releases word-timestamped Sherlock recalls (DOI 10.5281/zenodo.8208709). Proposed interpretation: no new participant-consent/REB or redistribution-permission gate for local analysis; raw content remains outside Git and is neither redistributed nor remotely processed. Retain only scientific reproducibility requirements needed to make the target canonical: published-source identity, local artifact binding, explicit transforms/timebases, separation of 1,000 microsegments / 50 Chen scenes / 30 outcome-tuned HMM events, and predeclared validation. Candidate cand-13MABH3J3CKW7M5CV3QZQ7PREZ no longer reflects owner intent despite one approval; please stop reviewing it. Chief guidance requested on the revised status and exact successor wording before I publish a replacement candidate. No admission or landing claim.
